business_problem: TTI's legacy software and ad hoc tooling could not scale to the geospatial and IoT volumes generated by connected vehicles, cameras, weather and roadway datasets, limiting collaboration, governance and safety analysis.
solution_summary: Texas A&M Transportation Institute moved connected-vehicle, geospatial and external roadway data onto the Databricks Data + AI Platform on Azure so researchers could work with streaming safety data at the scale their legacy PCs and ad hoc tools could not handle. GPS points from millions of vehicles, weather feeds, roadway infrastructure data and crash datasets are ingested into a shared lakehouse, where Delta Lake stores the growing corpus and Unity Catalog manages access, lineage and data tracking across teams. Researchers use Databricks H3 grid indexing to subset location-based workloads, then publish flexible visualizations through Power BI and Tableau. The platform lets TTI build crash analytics, speed studies, telematics planning models and weather-driven transportation analyses without the manual bottlenecks that previously limited collaboration, governance and the ability to process trillions of points for agency clients.

data_flow: GPS points, traffic-camera data, roadway infrastructure, crash information and weather feeds are ingested into Databricks, stored in Delta Lake and governed through Unity Catalog. Researchers use H3-based geospatial processing to build transportation models and then publish targeted analyses through Power BI and Tableau for agencies and internal teams.
business_outcome: TTI can now unify hundreds of terabytes and trillions of GPS points, accelerate analysis for predictive crash and planning use cases, distribute reliable data to nontechnical teams and support safer roadway decisions without the scalability and governance limits of its old environment.

evidence_quotes: Today, connected vehicle information — generated by IoT sensors built into vehicles, traffic cameras and more — yields trillions of data points that must be combined with external data sources such as roadway infrastructure and weather information.
Capturing 19 months of data can easily surpass 150 terabytes or 1.2 trillion GPS points.
With Unity Catalog we can provide organization without being too controlling or burdensome, so we're facilitating data access, lineage and data tracking.

With Delta Lake, TTI has accelerated code development in a more streamlined environment and can more easily visualize geospatial data with flexibility based on client preferences using seamless integrations with Power BI and Tableau.
This allows TTI to layer different types of internal and external data for deeper analytics in support of specific client use cases.
